title: Monthly rain and temperature terms removed about half of the post-1997 eastern US runoff offset; the remaining deficit was in basins south of 39 N and mostly in November-April (CAMELS, 1951-2025)
abstract: Question: after 1997, runoff in the eastern US (East-US) and south-east Australia (SE-AU) fell about 40 mm per year below 1951-1996 annual rainfall-runoff relations. In which months is the runoff lost, and do monthly rain timing, monthly temperature or snow explain it? Approach: 655 catchments with complete monthly flow (CAMELS-AUS v2.03 to 2021 with AGCD and SILO rain; 244 East-US and 250 western US CAMELS gauges with USGS flow and nClimGrid to water year 2025). Per catchment and calendar month we fitted 1951-1996 models with annual rain (A0, A) or monthly rain and temperature lags (MnoT, M), with a cluster bootstrap and a nine-window time null. The plan was fixed before results; quarterly annual models and a 39 N split are post hoc. Results: East-US residuals in 2010-2025 were -41 mm/yr (A0), -37 (A) and -16 mm/yr with model M (95% CI -28 to -2; null -8 to +18). Monthly rain alone removed about 4 mm/yr; the temperature terms removed most of the rest, but quarterly annual models gave -20 to -42 mm/yr, so this half is not uniquely attributable. The deficit was largest in snow-poor basins (snow fraction < 0.10: -27 mm/yr with M) and absent in snowy ones (+8, CI -21 to +30). South of 39 N model M left -35 mm/yr (-50 to -16), 70% in November-April; north of 39 N it left +2 mm/yr. In SE-AU with AGCD rain the deficit stayed -37 to -52 mm/yr in all seven structures; rain timing explained at most 15%, and the loss was about 4-6 mm in most months, so fractional losses were largest at low flow. With SILO rain it fell to -16 mm/yr, inside the time null. Conclusion: snow loss and rain seasonality do not explain the post-1997 eastern US offset; its robust part is a dormant-season loss in southern basins. Limitations: the latitude split is post hoc, temperature coefficients may include weather-type effects, SE-AU results depend on the rain product, and causes were not tested directly.
